title: Romans Chapter 7 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Romans chapter 7 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Romans Chapter 7 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Romans Chapter 7.

questions.question: In Romans 7, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: The law hath dominion over a man
The woman which hath an husband
Ye also are become dead to the law
questions.correctAnswer: The law hath dominion over a man
questions.explanation: This is the first statement made in Romans 7, found in the first verse.

questions.question: According to Romans 7, how long is a woman bound to her husband by the law?
questions.explanation: This is stated in Romans 7:2, indicating the duration of the binding law.

questions.question: What happens to a woman if her husband is dead according to Romans 7?
options: She is still bound by the law
She is loosed from the law
questions.correctAnswer: She is loosed from the law
questions.explanation: Romans 7:2 explains that a woman is freed from the law of her husband if he is dead.

questions.question: What is said about a woman who marries another man while her husband is alive?
options: She is free from all law
questions.explanation: This is stated in Romans 7:3, indicating the consequence of such an action.

questions.question: What are believers said to be dead to by the body of Christ?
questions.explanation: Romans 7:4 states that believers are dead to the law by the body of Christ.

questions.question: What should believers bring forth unto God according to Romans 7?
questions.explanation: This is directly mentioned in Romans 7:4 as the purpose of being married to Christ.

questions.question: What worked in the members of those in the flesh according to Romans 7?
questions.explanation: Romans 7:5 states that the motions of sins worked in the members to bring forth fruit unto death.

questions.question: What are believers now delivered from according to Romans 7?
questions.explanation: Romans 7:6 states that believers are delivered from the law.

questions.question: What does Romans 7:7 say about the law?
questions.explanation: Romans 7:7 clarifies that the law helps us recognize sin, including lust.

questions.question: What did sin do according to Romans 7:8?
options: It took occasion by the commandment
questions.correctAnswer: It took occasion by the commandment
questions.explanation: This phrase is found in Romans 7:8, indicating how sin exploits the commandment.

questions.question: What happened to Paul when the commandment came according to Romans 7:9?
questions.explanation: Romans 7:9 states that when the commandment came, sin revived, and Paul died.

questions.question: Is the law sin according to Romans 7?
questions.explanation: Romans 7:7 states 'God forbid' when questioning if the law is sin, indicating it is not.

questions.question: Did Paul know lust before the law according to Romans 7?
questions.explanation: Romans 7:7 indicates that Paul did not know lust except through the law.

questions.question: According to Romans 7, sin was alive without the law forever.
questions.explanation: Romans 7:8 states that without the law, sin was dead, not alive.

questions.question: According to Romans 7:6, believers serve in the oldness of the letter.
questions.explanation: Romans 7:6 states that believers serve in newness of spirit, not in the oldness of the letter.

medium.title: Romans Chapter 7 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Romans Chapter 7 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Paul find the commandment, which was ordained to life, to be?
questions.explanation: This is correct as stated in Romans 7:10, where Paul says he found the commandment to be unto death.

questions.question: What does Romans 7:11 say about sin in relation to the commandment?
questions.explanation: Romans 7:11 explains that sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived Paul and slew him.

questions.question: How does Paul describe the law and commandment in Romans 7:12?
questions.explanation: In Romans 7:12, Paul states that the law is holy, and the commandment is holy, just, and good.

questions.question: In Romans 7:13, what does Paul clarify about the law and death?
questions.explanation: Romans 7:13 clarifies that it is sin that works death in Paul by that which is good, making sin appear exceedingly sinful.

questions.question: What does Romans 7:14 say about the nature of the law?
questions.explanation: According to Romans 7:14, the law is spiritual, but Paul describes himself as carnal, sold under sin.

questions.question: According to Romans 7:15, what struggle does Paul express regarding his actions?
options: He always does what is right
He does not do what he allows
questions.explanation: In Romans 7:15, Paul admits that he does what he hates, indicating a struggle with his actions.

questions.question: What does Romans 7:16 indicate about Paul's consent regarding the law?
options: He consents that the law is good
He believes the law is dead
questions.correctAnswer: He consents that the law is good
questions.explanation: Romans 7:16 states that if Paul does what he would not, he consents unto the law that it is good.

questions.question: In Romans 7:17, who does Paul attribute his sinful actions to?
questions.explanation: Paul explains in Romans 7:17 that it is no longer he who does it, but sin that dwells in him.

questions.question: What does Romans 7:18 reveal about Paul’s understanding of his own nature?
options: There is no good thing in his flesh
questions.correctAnswer: There is no good thing in his flesh
questions.explanation: Romans 7:18 reveals that Paul recognizes that in his flesh dwells no good thing.

questions.question: What does Romans 7:4 say about believers and the law?
options: They are bound by the law
They are dead to the law
questions.correctAnswer: They are dead to the law
questions.explanation: Romans 7:4 states that believers are become dead to the law by the body of Christ.

questions.question: According to Romans 7:5, what was the result of being in the flesh?
options: It brings forth fruit unto life
It brings forth fruit unto death
questions.correctAnswer: It brings forth fruit unto death
questions.explanation: Romans 7:5 explains that when they were in the flesh, the motions of sins brought forth fruit unto death.

questions.question: What does Romans 7:6 say about the state of believers now?
options: They are still under the law
They are delivered from the law
questions.correctAnswer: They are delivered from the law
questions.explanation: Romans 7:6 states that believers are delivered from the law, serving in newness of spirit.

questions.question: True or False: According to Romans 7:11, sin can use the commandment to deceive.
questions.explanation: This is true as Romans 7:11 states that sin took occasion by the commandment and deceived Paul.

questions.question: True or False: In Romans 7:12, Paul states that the commandment is a burden.
questions.explanation: This is false because Romans 7:12 describes the commandment as holy, just, and good, not as a burden.

questions.question: True or False: Romans 7:14 indicates that the law is carnal.
questions.explanation: This is false; Romans 7:14 states that the law is spiritual, contrasting it with Paul's carnal nature.

hard.title: Romans Chapter 7 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Romans Chapter 7.

questions.question: According to Romans 7:19, what does Paul say about his actions concerning good and evil?
options: He does the good he wants but not the evil
He does neither good nor evil
He does not do the good he wants but does the evil he does not want
He always does what he desires
questions.correctAnswer: He does not do the good he wants but does the evil he does not want
questions.explanation: Romans 7:19 states, 'For the good that I would I do not: but the evil which I would not, that I do.' This clarifies Paul’s struggle with doing good versus evil.

questions.question: In Romans 7:20, Paul says that if he does what he would not, who is responsible for that action?
questions.explanation: Romans 7:20 says, 'Now if I do that I would not, it is no more I that do it, but sin that dwelleth in me,' indicating sin’s indwelling power causes the action.

questions.question: What does Paul find when he tries to do good according to Romans 7:21?
questions.explanation: Romans 7:21 says, 'I find then a law, that, when I would do good, evil is present with me,' showing the internal conflict within Paul.

questions.question: Romans 7:22 describes Paul's attitude toward the law of God. What is it?
questions.explanation: Romans 7:22 states, 'For I delight in the law of God after the inward man,' indicating an inward appreciation of God's law.

questions.question: According to Romans 7:23, what is the nature of the conflict Paul describes?
options: A law in his members warring against the law of his mind
A conflict between Paul and his neighbors
questions.correctAnswer: A law in his members warring against the law of his mind
questions.explanation: Romans 7:23 says, 'But I see another law in my members, warring against the law of my mind,' describing the internal spiritual struggle.

questions.question: In Romans 7:24-25, Paul expresses a cry of despair and then a note of thanksgiving. What is he thankful for?
questions.explanation: Romans 7:25 says, 'I thank God through Jesus Christ our Lord,' showing that deliverance from the 'body of this death' comes through Christ.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'νοῦς' (nous) in Romans 7:25 mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word 'νοῦς' in Romans 7:25 is translated as 'mind' indicating the faculty of understanding or reason.

questions.question: Which literary device best describes the conflict between 'the law of my mind' and 'the law of sin in my members' in Romans 7:23?
questions.explanation: Romans 7:23 personifies 'law' as warring forces within Paul, showing internal struggle through personification.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage shares the theme of inner conflict with sin as expressed in Romans 7:14-25?
questions.explanation: Psalm 51:3-5 expresses a recognition of sinfulness and inner conflict, paralleling Romans 7:14-25’s theme of struggle with sin.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes Paul's cry 'O wretched man that I am!' in Romans 7:24 about deliverance from sin?
questions.explanation: Romans 8:1-2 follows Romans 7:24 with the declaration of no condemnation and life through the Spirit, answering the cry for deliverance.

questions.question: What comes immediately before Romans 7:19, where Paul says he does not do the good he wants?
options: He says that sin dwells in him
He declares the law is good
He describes his delight in the law
questions.correctAnswer: He says that sin dwells in him
questions.explanation: Romans 7:18 precedes 7:19 and says, 'For I know that in me (that is, in my flesh,) dwelleth no good thing,' setting up the struggle in verse 19.

questions.question: In Romans 7:7-8, Paul discusses the role of the law. What concept does he introduce about sin in relation to the law?
options: Sin is independent of the law
Sin is dead without the law
Sin is only in the heart
questions.correctAnswer: Sin is dead without the law
questions.explanation: Romans 7:8 states, 'For without the law sin was dead,' showing sin’s activation through the law.

questions.question: How does Paul describe the law in Romans 7:12?
questions.explanation: Romans 7:12 says, 'Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy, and just, and good,' affirming the law's perfect nature.

questions.question: Romans 7:4 uses a metaphor involving marriage to explain our relationship to the law. What is the key point of this metaphor?
options: We are married to sin forever
We are dead to the law through Christ and married to Him
The law is like a contract
questions.correctAnswer: We are dead to the law through Christ and married to Him
questions.explanation: Romans 7:4 explains believers are 'dead to the law by the body of Christ; that ye should be married to another,' illustrating freedom from the law.

questions.question: True or False: According to Romans 7:15, Paul hates what he does.
questions.explanation: Romans 7:15 says, 'For that which I do I allow not: for what I would, that do I not; but what I hate, that do I,' confirming the statement is true.

theological.title: Romans Chapter 7 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Romans Chapter 7 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Romans 7:4 teach about the believer's relationship to the law and Christ?
options: Believers are dead to the law by the body of Christ and married to Him to bear fruit unto God
Believers remain under the law but are justified by faith in Christ
The law is abolished completely for believers once they accept Christ
Believers must obey the law perfectly to remain in union with Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Believers are dead to the law by the body of Christ and married to Him to bear fruit unto God
questions.explanation: Romans 7:4 teaches that believers have died to the law through the body of Christ so that they might be joined to Christ, who was raised from the dead, to bear fruit for God.

questions.question: What doctrine concerning sin and the law is taught in Romans 7:7?
options: Sin is known only through the law, which reveals what is forbidden
The law causes sin to exist in humanity
Sin is independent of the law and would exist without it
The law itself is sinful and corrupts the conscience
questions.correctAnswer: Sin is known only through the law, which reveals what is forbidden
questions.explanation: Romans 7:7 states that sin was not known except through the law, specifically through the commandment 'Thou shalt not covet,' showing the law's role in revealing sin.

questions.question: What doctrine is expressed in Romans 7:14 about the nature of the law and the human condition?
options: The law is spiritual, but humans are carnal and sold under sin
The law is carnal and unable to govern the spiritual man
Humans are spiritual and therefore not subject to the law
The law is obsolete because humans are spiritual
questions.correctAnswer: The law is spiritual, but humans are carnal and sold under sin
questions.explanation: Romans 7:14 clearly teaches that the law is spiritual in nature, but the speaker identifies himself as carnal, sold under sin, emphasizing human weakness despite the law's holiness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Romans 7:12 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Romans 7:12 declares the law and commandments to be holy, just, and good, reflecting God's attribute of holiness.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Romans 7:25 when Paul thanks God through Jesus Christ our Lord?
questions.explanation: Romans 7:25 shows Paul thanking God through Jesus Christ for deliverance, demonstrating God's grace as the means of salvation from sin's bondage.

questions.question: How does Romans 7 prepare the way for the teaching in Romans 8 regarding life in the Spirit?
options: By diagnosing the inner conflict and inability to fulfill the law, it sets the need for the Spirit's empowerment
By teaching that legalism is sufficient for sanctification
By denying any struggle with sin after conversion
By emphasizing that the law is the final means of salvation
questions.correctAnswer: By diagnosing the inner conflict and inability to fulfill the law, it sets the need for the Spirit's empowerment
questions.explanation: Romans 7 shows the believer's struggle with sin despite the law, thus preparing for Romans 8 where life in the Spirit enables victory over sin.

questions.question: How does the description of being 'dead to the law' in Romans 7:4 connect to the Old Testament covenantal themes?
options: It echoes the idea of dying to the old covenant to enter a new covenant in Christ
It suggests the Mosaic covenant remains the only valid covenant
It implies the law is eternal and unchangeable
It denies any continuity between the Old and New Covenants
questions.correctAnswer: It echoes the idea of dying to the old covenant to enter a new covenant in Christ
questions.explanation: Romans 7:4 uses marriage and death imagery that aligns with covenantal theology, showing believers have died to the law covenant to be joined to Christ in a new covenant.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Romans 7:17 and 7:20 teach about sin and the believer's agency?
options: Sin dwells in believers and acts through them, but the believer is distinct from the sin
Believers are completely passive and not responsible for sin
Sin only affects the unbeliever and not the believer
Believers do all sin acts personally and without any external influence
questions.correctAnswer: Sin dwells in believers and acts through them, but the believer is distinct from the sin
questions.explanation: Romans 7:17 and 7:20 show that sin dwells within and acts through the person, yet the 'I' is distinguished from the sin, indicating a complex inner struggle with sin's presence.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about the law and inner conflict is taught by Romans 7:21 and 7:23?
options: There is a law of sin in the members warring against the law of the mind, causing captivity
The law of God is ineffective and powerless to convict sinners
There is no real contradiction between mind and flesh
Sin is external and does not affect the believer's mind
questions.correctAnswer: There is a law of sin in the members warring against the law of the mind, causing captivity
questions.explanation: Romans 7:21 and 7:23 describe the internal warfare between the desire to obey God's law and the sinful nature in the body that leads to spiritual captivity.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about the law and sin is taught by Romans 7:9 and 7:11?
options: The commandment intended for life actually worked death because sin deceived and killed through it
The law itself is the cause of death and sin
Sin was powerless before the law was given
The law automatically sanctifies those who keep it
questions.correctAnswer: The commandment intended for life actually worked death because sin deceived and killed through it
questions.explanation: Romans 7:9 and 7:11 explain that though the commandment was meant to bring life, sin used it as an opportunity to deceive and bring death.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Romans 7:14-25 teaches that the law is sinful and condemns God’s law as evil. What does Romans 7:14-25 actually teach?
options: The law is holy and good, but human sinfulness causes inner conflict and inability to fully obey
The law itself is sinful and must be rejected
Paul denies the existence of sin and the law
The law fully empowers believers to overcome sin without assistance
questions.correctAnswer: The law is holy and good, but human sinfulness causes inner conflict and inability to fully obey
questions.explanation: Romans 7:14-25 shows Paul affirming the holiness of the law while describing his personal struggle with sin that dwells in his flesh, demonstrating the law's goodness but human incapacity.

questions.question: What doctrine about sanctification does Romans 7:6 teach?
options: Believers serve God in newness of spirit, not under the oldness of the letter
Sanctification is achieved by strict adherence to the letter of the law
The law remains the primary means of sanctification
questions.correctAnswer: Believers serve God in newness of spirit, not under the oldness of the letter
questions.explanation: Romans 7:6 teaches that believers are delivered from the law to serve God in a new spiritual way, contrasting with the old letter of the law.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is demonstrated by the law’s role in revealing sin as described in Romans 7:8?
questions.explanation: Romans 7:8 shows the law exposing sin’s deceitful power, reflecting God’s omniscience in making known what is hidden within human hearts.

questions.question: What doctrine about human inability and the will is taught in Romans 7:18?
options: The flesh contains no good thing; the will to do good is present but the ability to perform it is not found
The will and ability always work together perfectly in believers
Human flesh is inherently good and able to fulfill the law
There is no conflict between desire and action in the believer
questions.correctAnswer: The flesh contains no good thing; the will to do good is present but the ability to perform it is not found
questions.explanation: Romans 7:18 describes the paradox of desiring to do good but lacking the power in flesh to perform it, emphasizing human inability apart from divine aid.

questions.question: How does Romans 7:5 contribute to the overall biblical narrative of sin’s power before Christ?
options: Sin worked through the law to bring death while we were in the flesh, illustrating the curse prior to Christ’s redemption
Sin had no effect before Christ’s death
The law empowered believers to overcome sin before Christ
Sin was less powerful than grace before Christ
questions.correctAnswer: Sin worked through the law to bring death while we were in the flesh, illustrating the curse prior to Christ’s redemption
questions.explanation: Romans 7:5 shows how sin exerted power through the law resulting in death before believers were united to Christ, fitting the biblical theme of the law’s curse before grace.
